reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Reconstructed the exact English People Management pathway from the current track page and freshly retrieved adopted Appendix I, re-read the shared general regulations and the 2026 causal-analysis entry, then compared the frozen curricula and each positive alignment with the actual course evidence. This separate analytical pass was performed by the same AI, not an independent person.
findings: The normalized target is the English People Management track, not Dutch Personeelwetenschappen. The public page explicitly labels the 2026-entry curriculum and agrees with the adopted English table. Thirteen first-year units total sixty EC. Ten second-year units total sixty. Comparative Labor Relations, Social Philosophy, Cross-Cultural HRM, the twelve-credit thesis and thirty open credits complete year three. GROW remains non-credit.

The shared general OER supplies a 120 EC bachelor-thesis entry threshold and the forty-two-credit ordinary BSA. The track-specific appendix gives no further thesis gate. The selected full first two years meet the thesis threshold. The open window permits approved placement, minor and elective combinations; no particular combination or internship is selected. Its underlying subject content remains open. No retrieval uncertainty is represented as a completed course or invented credit.

The thirteen direct interests support international people management, organisational psychology, talent and well-being, analytics and cross-cultural and labour questions. The closest option develops organisational, leadership, finance and empirical reasoning. The psychology option deepens health, development and evidence synthesis, with clinical courses bounded as psychological-health foundations. The institutional option connects EU and international law, policy, economics and organisations with survey inquiry and econometrics. It does not promise employment-law or talent-management specialisation.

Re-read the 2026 Causal Analysis Techniques entry shared with GMSI: linear regression and empirical statistical interpretation support partial alignment to Econometrics, while the different techniques and applications remain explicit. Tilburg requires an SPSS skills pass as well as the written exam. Other positive alignments share identifiable primary content or method. Clinical assessment, general law and ethics remain unmatched to talent, comparative labour relations and philosophy of science. Optional research remains outside scheduled credits.

All three revised schedules pass offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, twenty-four unique courses, four per semester, first-year PPD and the advanced-course floor. Research methods precedes behavioural statistics under the advisory sequencing preference. Pairwise curricular differences are substantive. Read twenty-eight external titles, five note anchors, three concepts, the limitation note, source and UCR links and thirty-nine selected description texts. All audience references select the intended content under normal presentation.
